edition.alertText: OPEC+ holds December output targets unchanged; Brent settles $117.64 (+2.4%) on Oct 30 — highest since April; IRGC claims two tankers hit mines Nov 1; Sinokor PGSA ban takes effect Nov 1; Trump says war ending 'one way or the other' — no strikes before midterms; Araghchi proposes 2-day Hormuz reopening plan via Qatari mediators; Khamenei orders 'maximum deterrence' and response 'without geographical limitations'; Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda struck near Hormuz; UKMTO: 30+ attacks in October — double September's total; Louise 1 hit by limpet mines near Khasab; RITI tanker fire evacuated by Oman; Saudi intercepts 4 Houthi drones over Medina, Riyadh; Houthis strike Aden presidential palace; Iran army warns new war could last longer; Rubio: Trump 'hasn't made a decision' on strikes; UAE braces for worst

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis entered day 246 with overlapping diplomatic overtures and intensifying maritime violence ahead of the November 3 US midterms. OPEC+ held December oil output targets unchanged at its November 1 online meeting, with the seven core producers acknowledging that actual supply remains well below quotas — Argus estimated September output at 30.24M b/d against a combined target of 34.45M b/d, a 4.21M b/d shortfall. The decision was widely expected; Rystad's Jorge Leon called it 'the easy one,' noting the real challenge comes at the November 29 full meeting on 2027 baselines. On the diplomatic front, Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi proposed a compressed two-day Hormuz reopening plan through Qatari mediators — requiring US compliance measures on day one and Iranian strait reopening on day two — while insisting Iran has 'no plans currently for meetings with US officials.' Qatari mediators held 12+ hours of talks with Iranian officials in Tehran (Oct 30) and Doha (Oct 31), but no agreement to resume direct US-Iran negotiations emerged. Trump said the war will end 'very soon, one way or the other' while signaling no strikes before midterms, and Secretary of State Rubio confirmed Trump 'hasn't made a decision' on resuming military action. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei convened military chiefs and ordered 'maximum deterrence' with responses 'without geographical limitations,' while commanders reported raised readiness across the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf of Oman.

Oil prices surged on Friday before pulling back into Monday trading. Brent crude settled at $117.64 on October 30, up $2.76 (+2.4%) — the highest level since late April — as fears of renewed US strikes after the midterms combined with supply concerns. WTI climbed toward $104 on the same session. However, by Monday November 2, Brent fell to around $111.11 (-2.0%) and WTI dropped to about $101.71 (-2.3%) as investors weighed diplomatic signals against military risks. Brent has risen roughly 15% in October, marking a fourth consecutive monthly gain, and is up over 70% year-over-year. Gold traded around $3,900/oz after retreating from recent highs. ExxonMobil reported third-quarter profit more than doubled to $15.4 billion on the energy surge. The OPEC+ freeze matters less than it appears because actual supply is well below quotas, with output 3.16M b/d below February's pre-war level. War-risk insurance premiums reached 7.5–10% of hull value per Hormuz transit in October — for a $100M VLCC, that means $7.5–10M per passage versus $250,000 pre-war.

The maritime front saw continued escalation over the weekend. On Friday October 30, the Panama-flagged tanker Louise 1 was hit by two limpet mines about 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab — Bloomberg called it the first confirmed successful limpet mine strike in the strait since the war began. The Panama-flagged tanker RITI caught fire in the strait the same day; Oman's Maritime Security Centre rescued all 25 crew. UKMTO counted just over 30 attacks in October, twice September's total and the worst month for shipping since the war began. On November 1, the IRGC claimed two more oil tankers exploded after hitting mines, alleging the crews had switched off navigation systems for an 'unauthorized, covert passage.' A UKMTO report at 15:09 UTC on November 1 described a vessel Mayday over VHF Channel 16 reporting a strike by an 'unknown projectile.' The Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda was struck by 'unidentified objects' on Friday evening. The PGSA ban on Sinokor's entire fleet took effect November 1 — Sinokor moved about 37% of Hormuz crude volume in September and its VLCC share topped 50% in early October, so enforcement would severely disrupt tanker capacity. CENTCOM's Admiral Brad Cooper said Iran's navy is 'at the bottom of the sea' and the US has helped Gulf partners export over 1.5 billion barrels of crude since summer. Saudi air defenses intercepted four drones over Medina, Riyadh, and southern Saudi Arabia, while Houthis fired ballistic missiles at the Aden presidential palace. The US military death toll from the war rose to 23.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne feeding into phosphate production costs — Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic idling South Fort Meade phosphate plant (Florida) for 6+ months from Dec 8 — 199 workers laid off due to sulfur shortage. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz remain near zero since early September (WTO Hormuz Trade Tracker). Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). UNCTAD's de la Mora warned at Doha forum (Oct 25) that farmers cutting fertilizer will hit 2027 crops; World Bank: fertilizer prices surging as Hormuz disruptions tighten supplies. Urea-to-corn ratio at 126 bushels/tonne vs 75 in Dec 2025 (CSIS). IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude.

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Edison: 3 more cargoes cancelled for Italy. Dutch TTF gas surges to €97.53/MWh (~$108.51), highest since 2022 energy crisis. Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda struck near Hormuz (Oct 31). Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Europe and Asia face short-term supply heading into winter. Kpler: Asian LNG prices to rise amid simmering geopolitical tensions.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge.
